marks.gloss_en: the officer concedes he would not return a friend's greeting before a king of flesh and blood, for they would cut off his head; ומה אתה שהיית עומד לפני מלך בשר ודם שהיום כאן ומחר בקבר כך, אני שהייתי עומד לפני מלך מלכי המלכים הקדוש ברוך הוא שהוא חי וקיים לעד -- על אחת כמה וכמה
והלא דברים קל וחומר (= kv_melech_malchei_hamelachim) -- and at once the officer was appeased (33a.2)
at once the officer was appeased, and the pious man went home in peace
מאי טעמא? מתוך ששקולה כתחיית המתים -- the reason for the mishnah's placement
Rav Yosef: since it [the might of rains] is equal to the revival of the dead, therefore they fixed it in [the blessing of] the revival of the dead
מאי טעמא? מתוך שהיא פרנסה -- the reason for the mishnah's placement
Rav Yosef: since it [rain] is sustenance, therefore they fixed it in the blessing of sustenance
מאי טעמא? מתוך שהיא חכמה -- Rav Yosef's reason for the mishnah's placement
ורבנן אמרי: מתוך שהיא חול -- the Rabbis' reason for the mishnah's placement
Rav Yosef: since it [havdala] is wisdom, they fixed it in the blessing of wisdom
שנאמר כי אל דעות ה' -- 'knowledge' stands between two divine names
שנאמר כי לא עם בינות הוא על כן לא ירחמנו עושהו
Rav Ami: great is knowledge, for it was placed between two letters
שנאמר פעלת ה' מקדש ה' -- 'sanctuary' stands between two divine names
R' Elazar: great is the Temple, for it was placed between two letters
דעה נתנה בין שתי אותיות, מקדש נתן בין שתי אותיות -- R' Elazar's own ground for the equation
R' Elazar: any person who has knowledge -- it is as if the Temple was built in his days
שנאמר אל נקמות ה' -- 'vengeance' too stands between two divine names
מתקיף לה רב אחא קרחינאה: אלא מעתה, גדולה נקמה שנתנה בין שתי אותיות, שנאמר אל נקמות ה' -- if being placed between two divine names makes a thing great, vengeance too would be great
Rav Acha Karchina'a: but if so -- great is vengeance, for it was placed between two letters!
והיינו דאמר עולא: שתי נקמות הללו למה? אחת לטובה ואחת לרעה -- vengeance has a place where it is for good
לטובה -- דכתיב הופיע מהר פארן
לרעה -- דכתיב אל נקמות ה' אל נקמות הופיע
אמר ליה: אין, במילתה מיהא גדולה היא -- yes: in its place, at least, vengeance is great (a concession with a qualification; = p_nekama_gedola_bemilta), והיינו דאמר עולא
yes -- in its place, at least, it is great
the mishnah: one mentions the might of rains in [the blessing of] the revival of the dead
Rav Ami: great is knowledge, for it was placed at the start of the weekday blessings

ומה תפלה דעיקר תקנתא היא, אמרי: המבדיל בתפלה צריך שיבדיל על הכוס -- המבדיל על הכוס, דלאו עיקר תקנתא היא, לא כל שכן! -- the prayer, the principal enactment, still requires havdala over the cup as well; the cup, not the principal enactment, all the more requires havdala in the prayer as well (premise: p_mavdil_batefila_kos)

אמר רבא ומותבינן אשמעתין -- the tosefta does not send back one who omitted havdala in the prayer 'because he CAN say it over the cup': the cup is presented as an option, against the ruling that it is required
one who erred and did not mention the might of the rains in the resurrection blessing -- we send him back
לא תימא מפני שיכול לאומרה על הכוס, אלא אימא מפני שאומרה על הכוס -- read 'because he says it over the cup' (= p_emend_sheomrah_al_hakos)
do not say 'because he can say it over the cup'; rather say 'because he says it over the cup'

הא גופא קשיא -- the first clause implies the prayer alone suffices (אלמא תפלה לחודה סגי, = p_alma_tefilla_sagi); then once exempt by one, saying it in the other is a blessing that is not needed, which transgresses לא תשא -- how can the baraita bless one who says it in both?
so the prayer alone suffices [for havdala]
אלא אימא הכי: אם הבדיל בזו ולא הבדיל בזו ינוחו לו ברכות על ראשו (= p_emend_bezo_velo_bazo)
rather say thus: if he said havdala in this and did not say it in that, may blessings rest upon his head
the Men of the Great Assembly instituted for Israel blessings and prayers, kedushot and havdalot
at first they fixed it [havdala] in the prayer
one who said havdala over the cup -- what of his saying havdala in the prayer?
one who says havdala in the prayer is more praiseworthy than one who says it over the cup
Rav Chisda: one who erred in this and in that -- what is [the rule]?
the mishnah: even if a snake is wound on his heel, he does not interrupt [his prayer]
דתני רב הושעיה: מרחיקין משור תם חמשים אמה
דתני רב הושעיה: ומשור מועד -- כמלוא עיניו
R' Yitzchak: [one praying who] saw oxen -- he interrupts
מפני שהשטן מרקד לו בין קרניו
R' Meir: [when] the ox's head is in the basket, go up to the roof and throw the ladder from under you
מיתיבי: נפל לחפירה מלאה נחשים ועקרבים -- מעידין עליו שמת -- snakes kill one who falls among them, against Rav Sheshet's limiting the mishnah's 'he does not interrupt' to a snake
the baraita: [if] one fell into a lions' den, they do not testify that he died
שאני התם, דאגב איצצא מזקי -- there it is the pressure of his falling on them that makes them harm (= p_agav_itzetza_mazkei)
there it is different: by the pressure [of his falling on them] they do harm
an incident: an arvad was harming people; R' Chanina ben Dosa put his heel over its hole, it came out and bit him, and the arvad died; he carried it on his shoulder to the study hall
R' Chanina ben Dosa: see, my sons, the arvad does not kill; sin kills
at that hour they said: woe to the man whom an arvad meets, and woe to the arvad whom R' Chanina ben Dosa meets
